categories.title: Medical & Financial Relief
categories.summary: Verified help when an illness, debt or sudden financial crisis becomes too heavy for a family to carry alone.
categories.description: When a medical emergency or sudden financial hardship pushes a family beyond what it can manage alone, Amaana Foundation steps in with carefully verified, case-specific support. Depending on the need, assistance may help with urgent treatment costs, debt relief, livelihood recovery, or other essential financial burdens. Whether support is raised publicly or arranged privately, our focus remains the same: respond with dignity, use funds responsibly, and provide clear accountability for how assistance reaches the intended family.

categories.title: Emergency & Humanitarian Relief
categories.summary: From floods to community-wide emergencies, we respond with practical support, trusted local coordination and clear accountability.

categories.title: Ramadan & Eid Initiatives
categories.summary: Recurring programmes that turn the spirit of Ramadan, Eid and Qurbani into thoughtful support for families facing financial hardship.

categories.title: Amaana Taleem Initiative
categories.summary: Helping learners continue with dignity through educational essentials, Qur'anic learning and verified sponsorship pathways.
categories.description: Amaana Taleem Initiative brings together practical educational assistance and faith-based learning sponsorship for children and young people whose families may struggle to meet the cost of learning. The initiative began with identifiable, verifiable needs — including stationery kits for 50 orphan children in Borabanda, Hyderabad, in 2025 — and now also facilitates continuing sponsorship for Qur'an Nazira and Hifdh day scholars. As of September 2026, 25 students across Nazira and Hifdh were being sponsored through Amaana by multiple donors. As the initiative develops, Amaana also aims to extend verified support to school and college students whose education may otherwise be disrupted by financial hardship.

categories.title: Seasonal Relief & Essentials
categories.summary: Timely, practical support for seasonal needs that can place additional pressure on already vulnerable households.
categories.description: Amaana Foundation's Seasonal Relief & Essentials programme responds to predictable hardships that become more severe at particular times of the year. The focus is simple: identify a genuine seasonal need, reach people who are least equipped to absorb the added burden, and provide useful essentials at the time they are most needed. Winter support currently forms the programme's documented starting point, with future seasonal responses able to sit within the same framework as needs are verified.

initiatives.title: A Livelihood on Wheels
initiatives.summary: Sometimes the most meaningful assistance is not temporary relief, but the means to move forward independently. Through the collective support of our donors, ₹95,000 was raised to help provide an auto-rickshaw and essential start-up support—creating an opportunity for sustained income, greater stability, and a more dignified path forward.

initiatives.title: Together for a Newborn’s Recovery
initiatives.summary: In the first days of life, one family found itself facing an unexpected medical emergency. Their eight-day-old baby boy required hospital care and C-PAP respiratory support while mounting treatment costs placed the family under severe financial strain. Amaana Foundation mobilized a medical-aid appeal, and donors responded with compassion and urgency, helping raise ₹107,520 to support the family’s medical expenses. The child later improved and was discharged from hospital—a completed appeal made possible by timely community support.

initiatives.title: Standing With Him Through Cancer Surgery
initiatives.summary: Facing stage 3 oral cancer, a patient in Hyderabad required urgent surgery at Mythri Hospital in May 2025. Amaana Foundation mobilized community support for the medical need, and donors came together to contribute ₹319,000 toward his surgery. The appeal reflects what timely collective giving can achieve when a family is confronted with a serious medical crisis.

initiatives.title: Standing With Aliza Through Critical Care
initiatives.summary: Baby Aliza Fatima Quadri developed severe pneumonia that progressed to Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) with refractory hypoxemia, leaving her in need of advanced respiratory and intensive care. After High Frequency Oscillatory Ventilation (HFOV) was unable to stabilise her condition, she required veno-venous ECMO support, mechanical ventilation, IV antibiotics, and continued treatment in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit at KIMS Hospitals. Amaana Foundation mobilized an urgent medical-aid appeal and, through the generosity of donors, raised ₹482,700 toward her treatment. The Foundation team personally delivered the support to her family, who confirmed receipt and expressed their gratitude to everyone who stood with them during this critical period. At the time of the appeal update, Aliza remained under intensive treatment, so the fundraising appeal was completed while her medical recovery was still ongoing.

initiatives.title: Supporting a Mother Through Severe Burn Treatment
initiatives.summary: After suffering 45% severe burn injuries, a single mother of two required continued medical treatment at a time when her family had already exhausted much of its financial capacity. Around ₹4.2 lakh had already been spent on her care before the family approached Amaana Foundation for support. After reviewing the documents and verifying the case, Amaana mobilized a medical-aid appeal and raised ₹72,000. The amount was handed directly to the patient’s daughter to support the ongoing treatment need.

initiatives.title: Restoring Financial Breathing Room for an Auto Driver’s Family
initiatives.summary: An auto-rickshaw driver and father of two, was supporting his family on a modest and uncertain household income while living in rented accommodation. One son relied on irregular daily-wage work with no permanent employment, while his younger son had ongoing medical needs. Medical and household pressures had forced the family to pledge jewellery and take on debt, with interest continuing to increase the burden. After reviewing the loan paperwork and verifying the situation, Amaana Foundation chose to resolve the case privately rather than launch a public appeal. ₹138,300 was pooled by Amaana team members and friends, the outstanding loan was cleared, and the family’s pledged jewellery was released and returned.

initiatives.title: When Hyderabad Flooded, Our Community Responded
initiatives.summary: In October–November 2020, during Amaana’s early grassroots phase and before the Foundation was formally registered, the team responded to families affected by the Hyderabad floods through a three-phase relief effort. Support included ration and expanded relief kits, direct assistance to affected households, and coordinated help through trusted local organisations. Across the first two phases, 82 ration kits were distributed in Baba Nagar and Balapur and a further 60 expanded relief kits were provided for assessed flood-affected families, with Safa Baitul Maal supporting on-ground assessment and beneficiary coordination. A third phase included a designated ₹50,000 donor transfer for further relief support.

facts: Phase 1: approximately ₹125,000 raised; 82 ration kits worth approximately ₹60,000 distributed in Baba Nagar and Balapur.
Phase 1 also supported affected households directly and through HHF, Sakina Foundation, Deccanistan and Jamaat-e-Islami Hind.
Phase 2: 60 expanded relief kits worth over ₹100,000 handed to Safa Baitul Maal for assessed families.
Phase 3: a designated ₹50,000 donor contribution transferred to Safa Baitul Maal.
These activities were carried out by the founding team before formal registration. No exact unique-beneficiary total is available.

initiatives.title: Responding to Families During the COVID-19 Crisis
initiatives.summary: During the COVID-19 crisis in 2020, the family-led effort that would later become Amaana Foundation responded to households facing sudden income loss, food insecurity and severe uncertainty. Alongside the first Eid Gift Kits initiative, the founding team provided ration and essential-support assistance to families in need through its local community network.
initiatives.story:
During the COVID-19 crisis in 2020, the family-led effort that would later become Amaana Foundation responded to households facing sudden income loss, food insecurity and severe uncertainty. Alongside the first Eid Gift Kits initiative, the founding team provided ration and essential-support assistance to families in need through its local community network.

These early distributions took place before Amaana had formal organizational systems and standardized annual reporting. The work forms an important part of Amaana's grassroots history, but complete beneficiary and financial totals are not available today. Rather than reconstruct figures that cannot be verified, Amaana records the initiative honestly as part of its early emergency response.

initiatives.title: Sharing the Blessing of Iftar
initiatives.summary: Dates are a simple but meaningful part of Ramadan and the breaking of the fast. Through Amaana Foundation’s Dates Distribution initiative, this small act of giving has been carried forward year after year as part of our seasonal community support. Across the four documented years from 2023 to 2026, 420 kg of dates were distributed, with the programme growing from 78 kg in 2023 to 162 kg in 2026.

initiatives.title: Eid Gift Kits — Celebrating Eid With Dignity
initiatives.summary: Amaana Foundation’s Eid Gift Kits initiative is its longest-running annual programme, beginning in Ramadan 2020 as a family-led response during the COVID period in Hyderabad. Each year, carefully assembled household packages are provided to financially vulnerable families so they can prepare for Eid with greater dignity and ease. The contents and cost of each kit are adjusted to market conditions and household needs. From 85 families in 2020 to 710 families in 2026, the initiative has recorded 2,830 family distributions across seven annual drives.

initiatives.title: 2020 — Where the Eid Gift Kits Journey Began
initiatives.summary: In Ramadan 2020, during the uncertainty of the COVID period, the family-led effort that would later become Amaana Foundation began its Eid support programme by preparing and distributing gift kits to 85 families in Hyderabad. Each kit was valued at approximately ₹797 and contained practical household and festive essentials intended to help families prepare for Eid with dignity. This first drive became the foundation for what would grow into Amaana’s flagship annual initiative.

initiatives.title: Winter Drive 2025–26 — Warmth for Children and Vulnerable Families
initiatives.summary: During the 2025–26 winter season, Amaana Foundation carried out a multi-phase Winter Drive to provide practical cold-weather essentials to children and families facing winter without adequate protection. The support included sweaters, blankets and beanie caps and reached madrasa students, orphan children, widows, daily-wage labourers, domestic workers and other people in need.
initiatives.story:
During the 2025–26 winter season, Amaana Foundation carried out a multi-phase Winter Drive to provide practical cold-weather essentials to children and families facing winter without adequate protection. The support included sweaters, blankets and beanie caps and reached madrasa students, orphan children, widows, daily-wage labourers, domestic workers and other people in need.

In Phase 1, support was distributed at Al Madarsatul Islamia LiTahfizil Quranil Kareem, FeelKhana, Mallepally, reaching 96 madrasa students, including boys and girls from approximately ages 2 to 18 and underprivileged orphan children. In Phase 2, Amaana worked in collaboration with Al Khair Society at Al Khair Masjid, Hyderabad, where 101 Winter Kits were distributed. The phase records use different measures and are reported separately.
facts: These are separate phase measures, not one combined beneficiary total.
